title: Pokémon through the years
intro: One hundred moments in Pokémon: the games, the cards and the people who brought them to life.
dateNote: 100 selected milestones, 1996–2026. Dates refer to the region shown. Magazine entries use printed issue months unless an actual distribution date is given.

prelude.headline: Before Pokédex order
prelude.description: Guinness World Records identifies Rhydon as the first Pokémon character, designed by Ken Sugimori. Design order is separate from Pokédex order.

events.headline: Red and Green
events.description: Pokémon begins on Game Boy with Red and Green. Collecting and trading between versions are part of the original games.

events.headline: CoroCoro's Mew offer
events.description: CoroCoro invites readers to receive Mew in their game cartridges. Nintendo's developer interview recalls 20 winners and around 78,000 entries.

events.headline: Blue expands the first generation
events.description: A third Japanese version gives the original Kanto adventure a different presentation. Its availability begins through CoroCoro, before a later general retail release.

events.headline: The card game begins
events.description: The first Pokémon card expansion and starter pack launch in Japan, bringing collecting, trading and battling from cartridges to printed cards.

image.caption: Original Japanese Pokémon card expansion pack and cards from the official archive

events.headline: Two cards inside CoroCoro
events.description: Glossy Ivy Pikachu and Jigglypuff arrive on a printed mount inside CoroCoro. Their blue backs face up; readers peel them off to reveal the fronts. These printed promos are distinct from the earlier Mew game-cartridge giveaway.
events.sourceLabel: CGC Cards: Ivy Pikachu variant guide

events.headline: Jungle, Fossil and Team Rocket
events.description: The early Japanese card game expands beyond its first release. Jungle, Mystery of the Fossils and Team Rocket introduce new cards and the distinctive Dark Pokémon label.

events.headline: Ash and Pikachu on television

image.credit: The Pokémon Company / Nintendo / Creatures / GAME FREAK

events.headline: Gym Leaders enter the card game
events.description: Gym-themed cards attach familiar Trainers’ names to their Pokémon. Japanese decks and expansions feature Brock, Misty and other Gym Leaders, making each collection feel linked to a particular Trainer.

events.headline: Entei and the Unown
events.description: The third Pokémon film centres on Molly, a mysterious Entei and the Unown. A familiar world is transformed by the girl’s imagination, drawing Ash and his friends into an unusual rescue.

image.caption: Official film still from Pokémon 3: The Movie

events.headline: Crystal on Game Boy Color
events.description: Crystal arrives in Japan for Game Boy Color. Its illustrated packaging places Suicune at the centre of this return to Johto.

events.headline: Celebi crosses time
events.description: Celebi brings time travel into the fourth Pokémon film. Ash meets a boy from the past, while a hunter’s pursuit turns a forest adventure into a struggle to protect its Mythical Pokémon.

image.caption: Official still from Pokémon 4Ever
image.credit: The Pokémon Company / Nintendo / Creatures / GAME FREAK

events.headline: Shining Mew, from the magazine
events.description: A sealed paper insert in CoroCoro’s May issue holds Shining Mew. The Japanese-only promo pairs Hironobu Yoshida’s artwork with a sparkling Cosmos Holofoil finish. The little sleeve becomes part of the collecting story, too.
events.sourceLabel: PokeBoon: Shining Mew issue and insert

events.headline: The VS series
events.description: The Japanese VS series places Gym Leaders and their Pokémon in the spotlight. Its Leader’s Pokémon half decks form a compact, recognisable chapter in the history of Japanese card releases.
